Here the limits of the numerator and denominator are ${lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\operatorname{csc}⁡(x)=\infty $ and ${lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\operatorname{cot}⁡(2x)=\infty ,$ respectively, so we have the indeterminate form $\frac{\infty }{\infty }.$

Applying L'Hopital's rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{cot}⁡(2x)} & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{[\operatorname{csc}⁡(x)]^{′}}{[\operatorname{cot}⁡(2x)]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{-\operatorname{csc}⁡(x)\operatorname{cot}⁡(x)}{-2{csc}^{2}⁡(2x)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡(x)\operatorname{cot}⁡(x)}{2{csc}^{2}⁡(2x)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{(\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)})(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)})}{2(\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡(2x)})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x){sin}^{2}⁡(2x)}{2{sin}^{2}⁡(x)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x){(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))}^{2}}{2{sin}^{2}⁡(x)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\cdot 4{sin}^{2}⁡(x){cos}^{2}⁡(x)}{2{sin}^{2}⁡(x)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{4{cos}^{3}⁡(x)\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡(x)}}{2\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡(x)}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}2{cos}^{3}⁡(x) \\  & =2{cos}^{3}⁡(0) \\  & =2\cdot 1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
